metaDescription: Six 24V cordless leaf blowers compared on CFM, air speed, battery capacity, runtime, weight and noise so you know what a small battery can really move.
expertTake: The Greenworks 24V 515 CFM with the 5.0Ah battery is our top pick because it moves the most air of any single-battery 24V blower here and charges over USB-C. The Greenworks 320 CFM kit is the value pick for patios and small yards. If you have an acre of oak leaves or wet, matted piles every autumn, skip 24V entirely and move to a higher-voltage or gas machine.
introParagraphs: A 24V cordless leaf blower is a light, quiet tool for patios, driveways, decks and small lawns. The category is crowded with big airflow numbers, but a small battery can only deliver so much power for so long, so the headline figures often describe a short burst, not a working session.

This guide explains how airflow and air speed combine, what the battery label really tells you, and how to match a blower to your property. The quick picks sit above, and the detailed reviews below show which machine suits which cleanup job.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 515 CFM Brushless Leaf Blower with 5.0Ah Battery
products.description:
This Greenworks combines a brushless motor with a turbo mode, pushing 515 CFM at 130 MPH from a single 24V pack. CFM is air volume and MPH is air speed, and a blower needs both: volume to move a pile and speed to lift matted leaves. At 515 CFM it moves roughly 60 percent more air than the 320 CFM Greenworks kit.

The 5.0Ah pack is the largest in the guide, giving about 20 minutes on high and 40 on low. That is the honest runtime, and it is why the headline volume is a burst figure rather than a marathon. A variable speed trigger and cruise control let you hold a steady setting, and the stated 61 dB is quieter than the 65 dB on the 270 CFM model.

The USB-C battery charges from common chargers, a convenience when traveling or sharing power banks. Keep the nozzle clear, rinse dust from the vents and store the pack indoors at partial charge. The tool-only version of this blower is the same machine without the battery.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want the most air from a single 24V pack and fast USB-C charging.
pros: 515 CFM is the highest single-battery airflow here
5.0Ah USB-C pack gives the longest runtime in the guide
Turbo mode gives instant boost for wet or stuck debris
Cruise control reduces trigger fatigue on long jobs
cons: 20 minutes on high is short for a large yard
Heavier than the compact turbine models
24V platform cannot match higher-voltage blowers on wet piles

products.name: Greenworks 48V (24V x 2) 585 CFM Brushless Leaf Blower
products.description:
This blower uses two 24V batteries in series to make 48V, which is how it reaches 585 CFM and 140 MPH, the most of any blower in this guide. Two packs double the voltage available to the motor, and brushless efficiency turns that into real airflow. That is the closest this class comes to gas-like performance.

The tradeoff is that it needs both batteries installed and costs more than the single-pack models. Against the 515 CFM Greenworks, it adds roughly 70 CFM and 10 MPH, which helps on wet leaves, and the stated 30 minutes on high is better than the single 5.0Ah pack's 20.

The shared 24V platform means the packs also fit other tools. Charge both before a big job, wipe vents after use and avoid leaving the batteries in a hot car. It is the choice if you want more than a patio blower but still prefer cordless.
products.bestFor: Owners of larger yards who want gas-like airflow from the 24V platform.
pros: 585 CFM and 140 MPH lead the group on raw output
Two 24V batteries double the voltage to the motor
Up to 30 minutes of high runtime on a full charge
Packs are shared with the wider 24V tool platform
cons: Needs two batteries installed, so it is heavier
More expensive than the single-pack blowers
Charging two packs takes longer between sessions

products.name: Greenworks 24V 270 CFM Handheld Leaf Blower with 3.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The 270 CFM unit is a compact brushless blower aimed at everyday cleanup of decks, driveways and garages. Its 130 MPH air speed is strong for its size, so it lifts light debris off hard surfaces well, though 270 CFM means it moves less volume than the 515 CFM and 585 CFM Greenworks models.

The maker claims up to 55 minutes of runtime on low, a longer figure than the 20 minutes on high of the 515 CFM model, because low speed draws far less power. A concentrator nozzle focuses airflow for tight corners, and cruise control holds the setting. It includes a three year warranty.

Charging uses a USB-C cable and a 30W charger, with a 165 minute recharge time. It is easy to store and quiet. Rinse dust from the vents and keep the nozzle clean. It is best on patios and small lawns, not piles.
products.bestFor: Patio, deck and small-yard cleanup where weight and runtime matter more than raw volume.
pros: Up to 55 minutes of runtime on a 3.0Ah pack
130 MPH air speed lifts light debris cleanly
Three year warranty on a compact brushless tool
Concentrator nozzle focuses air for tight corners
cons: 270 CFM is half the airflow of the 515 CFM model
Struggles with wet or matted leaf piles

products.name: Greenworks 24V 320 CFM Cordless Leaf Blower Kit
products.description:
This Greenworks trades speed for volume: 320 CFM but only 90 MPH, the lowest air speed here. Lower speed means it moves loose, dry debris well but cannot dislodge heavy or damp leaves the way the 130 MPH models can. It is built for patios and hard surfaces, as its own description suggests.

It is a simpler, older-style kit with a variable speed dial and a concentrator nozzle for tight spaces. The 2.0Ah battery is the smallest here, so expect short runs, and its volume is higher than the 270 CFM model while its speed is far lower.

Because it does not use a brushless motor, it will wear brushes over time, a maintenance difference from the brushless units. Keep the vents clear and charge the battery indoors. It is the sensible budget pick for small hard-surface jobs.
products.bestFor: Small patios and hard surfaces where low cost and simplicity beat speed.
pros: 320 CFM moves a good volume of loose dry debris
Simple variable speed dial is easy to use
Battery and charger included in the kit
Concentrated nozzle clears tight spaces
cons: 90 MPH air speed is the lowest here for matted leaves
Not a brushless motor, so brushes wear over time

products.name: LawnMaster CLBL2417A 24V MAX Axial Cordless Leaf Blower
products.description:
LawnMaster uses an axial flow design, a straight-through fan that moves air in a line along the tube for efficient volume. The maker claims up to 335 CFM and 100 MPH, giving it slightly more volume than the 320 CFM Greenworks kit and a higher speed at 100 MPH.

The label shows its 24V MAX rating is the unloaded peak, with a nominal voltage of 21.6V, which is the figure closer to real working voltage. A two-speed control with turbo boost is simple, and the stated 32 minutes of runtime refers to turbo mode.

At under 9 pounds it is the heaviest here, which shows over a long job. The kit includes a 4.0Ah battery and charger. Clean the intake and nozzle, and store the battery indoors. It suits owners who prefer an axial design and a two-speed trigger.
products.bestFor: Owners who want an axial design and simple two-speed control with a 4.0Ah pack.
pros: Axial flow design moves air efficiently in a straight line
Up to 335 CFM edges past the 320 CFM Greenworks
4.0Ah battery and charger are included
Turbo boost mode adds power when needed
cons: Under 9 pounds is the heaviest in this guide
Only two speeds, with no variable trigger
The 24V MAX label overstates the 21.6V nominal voltage

products.name: Sun Joe 24V-TB-CT Cordless Compact Turbine Leaf Blower
products.description:
This is the lightest blower here at under 4 pounds, built around a 350 watt motor and a turbine fan. A turbine fan spins fast to build speed, claiming 100 MPH at 280 CFM. It will chase light leaves, grass clippings and even dusting snow, but the small motor limits it to light work.

The tradeoff is runtime: up to 12 minutes, the shortest in the group, against 55 minutes on the Greenworks 270 CFM. That is fine for a quick deck or porch sweep and not a lawn cleanup. It has less airflow than the 515 CFM model by nearly half.

It is easy to store and light on the wrist. Keep the vents clear and recharge the battery after each session. Buy it for quick tidy-ups only.
products.bestFor: Quick porch, deck and garage sweeps where weight is the main concern.
pros: Under 4 pounds is easy on the wrist and shoulder
100 MPH from a compact turbine fan
Light snow and dust clear quickly
Easy to store on a shelf or in a drawer
cons: Runtime of up to 12 minutes is the shortest here
280 CFM is too little for lawn leaves
Small 350W motor bogs on wet debris

buyingCriteria.explanation: CFM is air volume and MPH is air speed. Volume moves a pile and speed lifts stuck debris, so a high number in only one is misleading. For loose dry leaves, volume dominates, while wet or matted leaves need speed. The Greenworks 515 CFM offers 130 MPH, while the 320 CFM kit offers only 90 MPH.

Amp-hours tell you how long the pack lasts, and a small pack drained by a high-power blower runs dry fast. Manufacturers quote runtime on the lowest speed, so assume far less at full power. The 5.0Ah Greenworks gives 20 minutes on high, the 3.0Ah gives up to 55 on low, and the Sun Joe lasts up to 12.

A 24V system is a light-duty platform, and the batteries are often shared with other tools. Nominal voltage is the real working figure, as the LawnMaster label shows with 21.6V versus its 24V peak. Pairing two 24V packs for 48V, as the Greenworks 585 CFM does, is the way to get more power.

A brushless motor has no carbon brushes to wear, runs cooler and uses battery energy more efficiently. A brushed motor is cheaper but wears and loses power over time. Check for brushless in the listing. The Greenworks 515, 585 and 270 CFM models are brushless, while the 320 CFM kit is not.

Blowing is a long, repetitive job, so weight and balance matter. A heavy battery pack shifts weight to the rear. The Sun Joe is under 4 pounds while the LawnMaster is just under 9. Choose the lightest option that moves enough air for your property.

Cordless blowers are much quieter than gas, and the best are around 60 dB. Lower noise helps with neighbors and local ordinances. Warranty length indicates confidence in the battery. The Greenworks 270 CFM carries three years and states 65 dB, and the 515 CFM states 61 dB.

specDecoder.meaning: Cubic feet per minute of air moved. It measures volume, which governs how much debris moves at once.
specDecoder.watchFor: Quoted at the nozzle in turbo mode. Real working airflow is lower.

specDecoder.meaning: Speed of the air as it leaves the nozzle. Higher speed lifts matted and wet debris.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some listings show only MPH. Compare against CFM so a fast but thin stream does not mislead you.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. Larger numbers give longer runtime at the same power draw.
specDecoder.watchFor: Runtime claims use low speed. High-speed runtime can be a third of the headline.

specDecoder.meaning: Max is the unloaded peak when fully charged, while nominal is the average under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 24V MAX label may be 21.6V nominal. Compare Ah and CFM instead.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor design using electronics instead of carbon brushes, giving higher efficiency and less wear.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 320 CFM Greenworks is not brushless. Look for the word in the listing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared CFM and MPH together for every model. The Greenworks 585 CFM at 140 MPH led, with the 515 CFM at 130 MPH next.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at Ah ratings and stated runtimes, noting which were on low speed. The 5.0Ah and two-pack options ranked highest for work sessions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and efficiency
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated brushless from brushed designs and noted turbo modes. The 320 CFM kit was scored lower on long-term wear.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and ergonomics
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights and controls. The Sun Joe under 4 pounds and the LawnMaster at nearly 9 pounds marked the extremes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and warranty
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted stated decibel levels and warranty periods. The Greenworks 61 dB and 65 dB models with three years were highlighted.

cards.label: Single pack
cards.text: Lighter and simpler, with enough power for patios and small lawns. Includes the Greenworks 515, 270 and 320 CFM, the LawnMaster and the Sun Joe.

cards.label: Dual pack
cards.text: Doubles the voltage for gas-like airflow, but weighs more and costs more. Here that is the Greenworks 585 CFM.

howToChoose.note: Pick single pack for light yard work and dual pack if you regularly face large or wet leaf piles.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High air speed above 130 MPH and a turbo mode, since wet leaves are heavy and stick to the surface.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 585 CFM at 140 MPH and the 515 CFM at 130 MPH with turbo are the best fits, while the 320 CFM at 90 MPH struggles.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a big yard or heavy leaf drops. The Greenworks 585 CFM and 515 CFM add power and runtime.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only clear patios. The Greenworks 320 CFM or Sun Joe does the job.

maintenance.why: Dust and leaves block cooling air. A brush keeps the motor from overheating.
Cracks reduce airflow. A clear nozzle keeps pressure and focus.

maintenance.task: Store the battery at partial charge
maintenance.why: Lithium cells age fastest when full or empty. Store indoors at about half charge.
A discharged pack can drop below its safe level. Top it up before shelving.
Dirt in ports causes poor charging. A quick blow-out avoids it.

faq.q: Is 24V enough for a leaf blower?
faq.a: For patios, driveways and small lawns, yes. For wet piles and large yards, a higher voltage or dual-pack model works better.

faq.q: How long does a 24V blower run?
faq.a: It depends on speed. Stated runtimes use low settings, so on high expect between one third and one half of the headline figure.

faq.q: Is CFM or MPH more important?
faq.a: Both matter. CFM moves volume and MPH lifts stuck debris. Look for balanced figures.

faq.q: Do I need a brushless motor?
faq.a: It is not required, but brushless runs cooler, lasts longer and uses battery more efficiently.

faq.q: Can I use a 24V blower on wet leaves?
faq.a: Only the strongest, such as the dual-pack model, handle them well. Low-speed units will push wet leaves around.
Within a brand, yes for Greenworks 24V models. Other brands use different connectors.
